title: Release readiness for reporting dashboard

metadata.project: Internal reporting dashboard for customer success teams
metadata.mainEvaluationFocus: End-to-end extraction of release tasks, decisions, risks, dependencies, updates, and recall answers.
metadata.notes: Includes threaded replies, tentative/noisy ideas, clear updates, and two recall checks.

messages.text: Can we use this thread to check what still has to happen before we show the reporting dashboard to the customer success leads next week?
The main report view is mostly there. Filters for date range and account owner work, but the empty state still looks rough.
Agree. We should clean up the empty state before the walkthrough because some teams will not have enough historical data yet.
The export button is still confusing. It says download everything, but it actually only exports the filtered rows.
Let’s rename that to export filtered results. We do not need full-account export for this release.
There is also the question of permissions. Right now any customer success manager can see all accounts in the demo environment.
For the pilot, I think we should restrict the dashboard to the accounts owned by the signed-in manager. Otherwise the demo sends the wrong message.
Dark mode would be nice eventually, but I would not touch it now.
I checked the pilot notes again. The customer success leads mainly care about account health, recent usage, and the owner filter. They did not ask for dark mode or full export.
Then we can explicitly leave dark mode and full-account export out of the pilot scope.
One risk: the account health score is still using last week’s mock calculation. It looks plausible but it is not the final formula.
We should label the score as preview data in the walkthrough unless the analytics service is ready before then.
The analytics service is meant to expose the real score endpoint tomorrow, but I have not seen the contract yet.
Can someone check with analytics whether the score endpoint and response shape are confirmed?
I can do that after standup. If they do not have the contract, we should keep the preview label and avoid presenting the score as final.
Quick update: I cleaned up the empty state copy and added the illustration. It now says there is not enough activity for the selected filters.
Nice. That means the empty-state work is done from my side.
I spoke to analytics. The endpoint will exist, but the response shape is not stable until Friday.
Okay, then for next week we keep the preview label on the score and do not depend on the final endpoint.
I can rename the export button today. It is just copy and one snapshot update.
Permissions are probably the only non-trivial bit left. We need to make sure managers only see their own accounts before the walkthrough.
@Collaboration, what are the main things still left before the pilot walkthrough?
Update from me: the export button now says export filtered results, and the snapshot is updated.
I also added the preview data label next to the account health score. It is visible in the report header.
@Collaboration, what did we decide to leave out of the pilot scope?

contextNotes: The team is preparing an internal reporting dashboard for a pilot walkthrough.
Several concrete release tasks are identified: empty state, export label, account permissions, preview label, analytics endpoint check.
Dark mode and full-account export are explicitly left out of pilot scope.
Later updates resolve or narrow several earlier items.
